displayName: NBD Pro — nightly Firestore backup stale > 26h

documentation.content:
The nightlyFirestoreBackup scheduled function hasn't emitted a success log line in more than 26 hours. The cron runs at 04:00 America/Chicago daily; missing two consecutive runs means restore capability may be compromised.

Investigation:
  1. `gcloud functions logs read nightlyFirestoreBackup --project nobigdeal-pro --limit 50`
  2. `gcloud scheduler jobs list --project nobigdeal-pro | grep nightlyFirestoreBackup`
  3. `./scripts/verify-backup.sh` to enumerate recent backup folders
  4. Confirm the function SA still has roles/datastore.importExportAdmin + roles/storage.objectAdmin on the backup bucket.

---
FIXED 2026-09-04. This policy could never be created: its filter named jsonPayload/textPayload fields, which are LOG-entry fields with no meaning in the METRIC filter a conditionAbsent takes, and it carried no metric.type at all. It now watches the free system metric logging.googleapis.com/log_entry_count for service "nightlyfirestorebackup". Tradeoff: this fires when the service stops logging ENTIRELY, not when one specific heartbeat line stops. For a cron whose only activity is its scheduled run these are the same event. Narrowing it further would need a user-defined log-based metric, which is the one chargeable option. Duration pinned to the 86400s (24h) maximum Google allows for an absence condition (was 25h — Google caps absence duration at 24h). SECOND REWRITE 2026-09-04: an absence condition CANNOT express "a daily cron stopped" — Google caps absence duration at 23h30m, which is shorter than the 24h gap between runs, so it would false-fire every single day. Instead this now matches the ERROR that backupFreshnessCron already emits when it finds the export stale (functions/backup-freshness.js:120, logger.error backup_freshness.stale). That alarm was already the only working one in the project; this turns its log line into a page.
